serialFormats.description: Legacy 10-character York serial (1971 - Oct 2004): four letters + six-digit sequence. Letter 1 = plant, letter 2 = month, letter 3 = year, letter 4 = item type (M = mfg. basic unit, P = purchased basic unit, S/T = low-side item, Y/Z = accessory). Year letters cycle every 21 years; this entry is the FIRST cycle (A = 1971 ... Y = 1991).
sources: York Serial Numbers ID - From History to October 2004 (York/UPG serial ID sheet, usair-eng.com/Serialnumber.pdf)
Parts Town - York Serial Number Lookup (partstown.com/cm/resource-center/guides/gd2/york-serial-number-lookup)
Building Intelligence Center - York HVAC age (building-center.org/york-hvac-age/)
PICKHVAC - York HVAC Age: Serial Number Decoding (pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/york/)
How To Look At A House - age of a York air conditioner or furnace from the serial number (2018)
notes: AMBIGUOUS BY DESIGN: the year letter repeats every 21 years (A = 1971 or 1992 ... N = 1983 or 2004). The decoder will also match the 1992-2004 entry and flag the result ambiguous; pick the cycle from the nameplate: R-22 units with an ANSI/AHRI standard year printed on the plate in the 1990s, a Simplicity board, or a 10 SEER/EER rating are the 1992-2004 cycle; units this old (1971-1991) are rarely still in service.
Months skip I and J (K = Sep, L = Oct, M = Nov, N = Dec). Year letters skip I, O, Q, U.

Only ADFM654321 is a source-stated example (Parts Town / InspectApedia state it decodes to April, 1976 or 1997). The other two examples are rule-derived fixtures, not nameplate photos - which is why confidence is medium, not high.
The item-type letter (position 4) is captured as [A-Z]; the York sheet lists M, P, S, T, Y, Z. Coleman (Wichita, W) and Luxaire/Fraser-Johnston products built by York used this same scheme.

serialFormats.description: Legacy 10-character York serial (1971 - Oct 2004), SECOND letter cycle: year letter A = 1992 ... N = 2004. Same layout as the 1971-1991 entry: plant letter, month letter, year letter, item-type letter, six-digit sequence.
sources: York Serial Numbers ID - From History to October 2004 (York/UPG serial ID sheet, usair-eng.com/Serialnumber.pdf)
Parts Town - York Serial Number Lookup
Building Intelligence Center - York HVAC age
PICKHVAC - York HVAC Age: Serial Number Decoding
How To Look At A House - age of a York heat pump from the serial number (2020): letter series repeated every 21 years
notes: Regex only admits year letters A-N (1992-2004); letters P-Y in position 3 can only be 1984-1991 and are handled by the 1971-1991 entry, so those serials decode unambiguously.

For A-N the 1971-1983 cycle also matches: disambiguate from the nameplate (R-22 Sunline 2000 / Predator D-series with a Simplicity board = this cycle). The format ended in October 2004 (last letter N = 2004).
ADFM654321 is the source-stated example (April 1997 in this cycle); NLNM123456 and WGJM000789 are rule-derived fixtures.

serialFormats.description: Current York / Coleman / Luxaire / Fraser-Johnston / Champion serial (October 2004 - present): letter, digit, letter, digit, six-digit sequence (e.g. W1G7123456). Position 1 = plant, positions 2 and 4 read together = year (1 + 7 = 2017), position 3 = month letter (A-H = Jan-Aug, K = Sep, L = Oct, M = Nov, N = Dec).
sources: PICKHVAC - York HVAC Age (example W1G7123456 = July 2017, Wichita)
Building Intelligence Center - York HVAC age (2nd and 4th positions = year, 3rd = month letter, used exclusively since 2004)
Parts Town - York Serial Number Lookup
Central Air Conditioner and Refrigeration - How to read York HVAC model and serial number (examples W0E4298223 = 2004, W1E0298223 = 2010)
How To Look At A House - York heat pump age (2020): W1D5... = 2015
York Central Tech Talk - How To Read York Serial Numbers (2011, distributor 'decoder ring' PDF)
notes: Year = (digit in position 2) x 10 + (digit in position 4), 2000-based: W1G7 = 2017, N2K3 = 2023, W0E4 = 2004. Pattern letter/digit/letter/digit cannot be confused with the four-letter legacy format.
Month letters skip I and J (K = Sep). Several third-party decoders describe this as 'A to N, skipping I and J' - the same map.
Nameplate: York/JCI plates print 'SERIAL NO.' directly under 'MODEL NO.'; Coleman, Luxaire, Fraser-Johnston and Champion plates use the identical scheme (all built by JCI Unitary Products).

Confidence is medium (many agreeing secondary decoders; the first three examples are source-stated, N2K3456789 is a rule-derived fixture). No manufacturer document or warranty lookup could be consulted in this session - a JCI warranty lookup on york.com would raise it to high.
Rumoured newer formats (e.g. 'S...E...' 2019+) could not be confirmed; 'S' as position 1 is the Source 1 parts plant code in this same format.

controls.name: York Simplicity / Simplicity LITE unit control board (UCB) LED flash codes
controls.description: Single-LED flash-code diagnostics on the York unit control board. Original Simplicity (Sunline 2000 / Predator D-series, ~1998-2009: LAST ERROR button, Modbus/BAS port, fault history) and Simplicity LITE (Z-series 3-12.5 t, ~2009-2015) use different flash tables; only states confirmed from a cited source are listed here.

likelyCauses: Failed unit control board
Board processor not running (check 24 VAC supply before condemning)
checks: Verify 24 VAC at the board R-C terminals and the board fuse
Cycle power once; if the LED stays steady with good supply, replace the UCB
faultCodes.source: York ZE036 Installation Manual 5188235-YIM-B-1016, 'Simplicity Lite Unit Control Board Flash Codes' (p.66)

checks: No fault stored; if the unit does not respond, check thermostat inputs (Y1/Y2/W1/W2/G) at the board
faultCodes.source: York ZE036 Installation Manual 5188235-YIM-B-1016, 'Simplicity Lite Unit Control Board Flash Codes' (p.66)

likelyCauses: Anti-short-cycle / minimum off-time delay in progress
Board waiting on a pending call (delay timers)
checks: Wait out the delay (typically a few minutes) and confirm the compressor starts
Verify the call is still present at the thermostat inputs
faultCodes.source: York ZE036 Installation Manual 5188235-YIM-B-1016, 'Simplicity Lite Unit Control Board Flash Codes' (p.66)
faultCodes.notes: The manual's condition text for this code was not fully visible in the search summary; causes are interpretive.

faultCodes.meaning: Compressors locked out because the low ambient switch is closed
likelyCauses: Outdoor ambient below the low-ambient switch setpoint (switch is normally open, closes at about 45 F, opens at about 55 F)
Failed/shorted low ambient switch or wiring
checks: Measure outdoor ambient; if above 55 F, ohm the low ambient switch - it should be open
Check the switch wiring to the UCB for a short to common
faultCodes.source: JustAnswer HVAC thread on York rooftop flash code 10 (secondary; cites the York manual description)
faultCodes.notes: LOW confidence - from a secondary source only; confirm against the flash-code table printed on the unit's control-box label or IOM.

diagnosticTips: The flash-code LED is on the unit control board in the control compartment; codes are counted as flashes between pauses.

Original Simplicity boards: press and release the LAST ERROR button once (within 5 s) and the LED replays the last five stored fault codes, most recent first; history is also readable over the Modbus/BAS port.

The complete flash-code table (and the separate Ignition Control Board flash codes on gas units) is printed in the unit installation manual, e.g. ZE036 IOM 5188235-YIM-B-1016 p.66 'Simplicity Lite Unit Control Board Flash Codes / Ignition Control Board Flash Codes', and on the label inside the control box.
Most lockouts clear by removing the thermostat call (or cycling 24 V control power) once the cause is corrected.

controls.name: Johnson Controls Smart Equipment (Simplicity SE) controller - SE-SPU1001/1002/1011/1012
controls.description: Microprocessor unit controller with on-board LCD and joystick (SE-SPU), optional SE-Mobile app / Verasys BAS; alarms are named text alarms (service and FDD alarms), not numeric codes. Fitted to York/Coleman/Luxaire Z-series and later rooftops from about 2014.

faultCodes.meaning: Low-pressure switch input open for the circuit; compressor locked out after repeated trips
likelyCauses: Low refrigerant charge / leak
Low airflow or dirty filters causing coil freeze
Failed LPS or open wiring
checks: Gauge the circuit: suction pressure vs. LPS trip point
Check evaporator airflow, filters, blower belt
Ohm the LPS with the circuit equalized
faultCodes.notes: LOW confidence: alarm name paraphrased from memory of the SE controls guide, not transcribed. Verbatim list: LIT-12011998 Smart Equipment Controls Technical Bulletin, Alarm appendix / Service alarms.

faultCodes.meaning: High-pressure switch input open for the circuit; compressor locked out after repeated trips
likelyCauses: Condenser fan failure or dirty condenser coil
Overcharge or non-condensables
Failed HPS
checks: Verify condenser fan(s) run and coil is clean
Gauge head pressure against outdoor ambient
Check HPS continuity when pressure is normal
faultCodes.notes: LOW confidence: paraphrased; confirm in LIT-12011998 Alarm appendix.

faultCodes.meaning: Evaporator freeze sensor / freeze stat indicates coil freezing; compressor circuit locked out
likelyCauses: Low airflow (filters, belt, dampers)
Low charge
Failed freeze sensor
checks: Measure evaporator airflow / static
Check suction pressure and superheat
Verify sensor resistance vs. temperature
faultCodes.notes: LOW confidence: paraphrased; confirm in LIT-12011998 Alarm appendix.

faultCodes.meaning: Supply-air temperature sensor reads open/shorted or out of range
likelyCauses: Unplugged or damaged SAT sensor
Wrong sensor type / wiring to the SE-SPU
checks: Ohm the sensor (10k NTC style) and compare with the resistance table in the SE technical guide
Check the sensor plug on the SE-SPU
faultCodes.notes: LOW confidence: paraphrased; confirm in LIT-12011998 Alarm appendix.

diagnosticTips: Use the SE-SPU's LCD and joystick (Alarms menu) or the SE-Mobile app / Verasys UI to read active and historical alarms; the alarm names are text, not numeric codes.

The verbatim alarm tables are in the Smart Equipment Controls Technical Bulletin LIT-12011998 (Alarm appendix: Service alarms and FDD alarms) and the Simplicity SE Controls Technical Guide (SE-SPU1001/1002/1011/1012); the 2-stage rooftop guide is 5127914-UTG-B-1116.
Verasys Alarms Summary Technical Bulletin (Smart Equipment RTU controller section) lists the same alarms as seen from the BAS.
Compressor lockouts are cleared from the Alarms / Details menu or by cycling power once the cause is corrected.

electrical.familyLabel: York single package rooftops 3-25 t (Sunline 2000 / Predator / Z-series)
electrical.controlVoltage: 24 VAC from the unit control transformer (line voltage to 24 V), fused on the unit control board

components.name: Unit control board (Simplicity / Simplicity LITE) or SE-SPU (Smart Equipment)
Compressor contactors, circuit 1 / 2
components.notes: York wiring legends label contactors 'M' (motor contactor); verify on the unit diagram.

components.name: Freeze stat / freeze sensor on evaporator (per circuit)
Circuit breaker (electric heat / optional unit disconnect)
Phase monitor (3-phase scroll units)
components.notes: Presence/standard-since year not confirmed for York; check the diagram.

components.name: Low ambient switch (compressor lockout below ~45 F)
components.notes: Referenced by flash code 10 on Simplicity boards.

safetyDevices: LPS (auto reset, board lockout after repeated trips)
sequenceOfOperation: Cooling: thermostat Y1 (and G) to the UCB -> after any anti-short-cycle delay the board energizes compressor contactor 1M and the condenser fan(s); the indoor blower runs on G (or after a short delay on the board). Y2 adds circuit 2 (2M). Economizer, when enabled and outdoor air suitable, is used as first-stage cooling before compressors.

Gas heating: W1 to the UCB -> ignition control (IGC) energizes the combustion-air motor, proves the pressure switch, runs the ignition trial, opens the gas valve; the indoor blower starts after the heat blower-on delay. W2 brings on high fire / second heat section. Limit or rollout opening drops the gas valve; rollout is manual reset.

Safety: an HPS/LPS/freeze-stat opening drops that circuit's contactor; repeated trips within one call cause a board lockout indicated by the LED flash code (Simplicity) or a named alarm (Smart Equipment).
notes: LOW confidence: designators and sequence are generic York packaged-unit practice from memory, NOT transcribed from an IOM wiring legend in this session. Use the legend on the unit's wiring diagram (inside the control-box door) as authoritative.
Smart Equipment units add SAT/RAT/OAT sensors, per-circuit pressure switch inputs and a BAS/Modbus/N2 port on the SE-SPU; thermostat inputs still land on R/C/G/Y1/Y2/W1/W2/OCC.
sources: Generic York rooftop wiring practice (memory) - to be replaced by the IOM wiring-diagram legend for ZF/ZJ/DM units

commonIssues.symptom: Unit dead or erratic - LED steady on / no heartbeat (Sunline 2000 / Predator with original Simplicity board)
likelyCauses: Failed original Simplicity control board (well-known field failure on 1998-2009 D-series units)
Blown board fuse from a shorted 24 V field wire
Transformer failure
checks: Verify 24 VAC at R-C and the board fuse
Check for a shorted thermostat cable or economizer wiring before replacing the board
If steady-on LED persists with good supply, replace the UCB (retrofit kits exist)

commonIssues.symptom: Compressors will not run in cool weather; flash code 10 on the board
likelyCauses: Low ambient switch closed (normal below ~45 F)
Failed low ambient switch
checks: Note outdoor ambient; above 55 F the switch should be open
Ohm the LAS and its wiring to the UCB
sources: JustAnswer York rooftop flash code 10 thread

commonIssues.symptom: Gas heat lockout / no ignition on rooftop
likelyCauses: Combustion-air pressure switch not proving (blocked flue, failed inducer/combustion motor, cracked hose)
Dirty flame sensor
Rollout switch tripped (manual reset) from heat-exchanger or burner problems
Gas valve or supply pressure problem
checks: Read the IGC flash code (separate table from the UCB)
Check inlet/manifold gas pressure
Verify pressure switch closes when the combustion motor runs; inspect flue and hoses
Clean the flame sensor and check the microamp signal
Inspect the heat exchanger if rollout has tripped

commonIssues.symptom: Low pressure / freeze lockouts on Z-series or SE-controlled units
likelyCauses: Dirty filters or slipping/broken blower belt (low airflow)
Low charge / leak
Economizer damper stuck open in cold weather
checks: Filters, belt tension, blower wheel
Suction pressure and superheat
Economizer minimum position and actuator operation

commonIssues.symptom: Smart Equipment unit runs but not to setpoint; sensor alarms on SE-SPU
likelyCauses: Failed or unplugged SAT/RAT/OAT sensors
Controller configured for the wrong mode (thermostat vs. sensor/BAS control)
Economizer or occupancy settings not commissioned
checks: Read the SE-SPU Alarms menu
Ohm sensors against the resistance table
Review the controller Setup / Details menus (control mode, setpoints, economizer enable)

commonIssues.symptom: Economizer not modulating / free cooling never used
likelyCauses: Failed actuator or economizer logic module
Bad outdoor enthalpy/dry-bulb sensor or changeover setpoint
Linkage disconnected
checks: Command minimum position and observe damper travel
Check 24 V and control signal at the actuator
Check the OA sensor and changeover setting

Model formats decode category, series letter and tonnage only; the positions after the tonnage (heat type/input, voltage, options) were NOT transcribed from a nomenclature page in this session and are left undecoded rather than guessed.

Control platforms are partial: only the Simplicity LITE LED states confirmed from the ZE036 IOM plus one secondary flash code, and paraphrased Smart Equipment alarm names flagged low. Simplicity Elite (Millennium), original Simplicity full flash table, IGC flash codes, JCI IQ boards and Sun Premier 25-80 t fault tables are not included - see 'unresolved' in the build report.
Electrical and common-issue sections are generic field practice from memory and are marked low/inferred; treat the unit's wiring-diagram legend as authoritative.
